biography.plain_text: Carla Bossi-Comelli is an Italian-born cultural philanthropist and museum advocate based in Switzerland. A former president of the World Federation of Friends of Museums, she created its Mexican federation and scholarship program. She also chairs Manhattan School of Music's International Advisory Board, supporting musicians, museum volunteers and cultural organizations across several countries.

long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Italy and raised in Argentina, Bossi-Comelli studied economics and sociology in Buenos Aires before completing postgraduate work in museology and museography in Mexico City. During three decades in Mexico, she founded the Mexican Federation of Friends of Museums. Within the international federation, she moved from secretary-general to president, organized congresses and created a scholarship program in memory of her husband, Luigi Bossi.

Music education became a second long-term focus. Bossi-Comelli joined Manhattan School of Music's board, developed its international advisory council and encouraged scholarship support for students from many countries. Her philanthropy includes more than $5 million in commitments to the school, where a performance studio bears her name. She remains chair of its International Advisory Board, a trustee emerita and an advisory-board member of the Venice International Foundation.
